You are a VERIFIER. Your job is to FALSIFY claims, not confirm them. These claims are about to be posted publicly on a colleague's pull request; a plausible-but-unproven claim is worse than none.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa

=== RULES ===
- READ-ONLY on the repo. No commits/pushes/PR comments. `gh api` GET calls allowed.
- DO NOT check out any branch.
- **Use the LIVE PR head: ref `pr/61-live` (5fe247c).** Ref `pr/61` (74e2b82) is STALE — several of these claims were made against it and the newer commit touched `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`, `protected-file-guard.yml`, `zephyr-results-sync.yml`, `testing.md`. State for each claim whether it still holds at `5fe247c`.
- Base for comparison: `8362b3c`.

=== VERDICT VOCABULARY (exact) ===
**PROVEN** (show evidence) · **PARTIALLY PROVEN** (mechanism proven, consequence doesn't follow — say which part) · **UNPROVEN** (say what would settle it) · **REFUTED** (show why).
Each claim: also give **"What would falsify this"** + whether you attempted it.

=== CLAIMS TO TEST ===

**C16.** `e2e/support/pages/BasePage.js` applies `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`_VALUE` via Playwright's `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders()`, which attaches the header to EVERY request the page makes — including third-party origins (Didomi, GTM, Contentful, Emarsys, CDNs) — not only the storefront origin. So an access-gate secret is transmitted to third parties on every run.
**Attack it:** (a) verify the actual API used at live head — is it `setExtraHTTPHeaders` on the page/context, or `route()`-scoped, or set per-`goto`? (b) Confirm Playwright's documented semantics for that API — check `node_modules/playwright-core` typings/source or bundled docs. (c) Does this storefront actually load third-party origins during these specific tests, or is the claim theoretical? If you can't establish (c), say so and downgrade the wording accordingly.

**C17.** `.env.sample` at `pr/61-live` sets `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL=zimm-service@zimmermann.com` (blank at base `8362b3c`) and both it and `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD` moved from `# scope:tier` to `# scope:shared`. And `.env.sample`'s own header states that `npm run env -- push shared` writes values as plaintext GitHub Environment **Variables** readable by repo collaborators.
**Attack it:** verify all three parts separately — the value change, the scope change, and what the header actually says about `push`/plaintext/who can read. Also check `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` for whether `scope:shared` keys are actually pushed and as Variables vs Secrets. Is the email a "secret" by this repo's own definition?

**C18.** `browserstack.yml` at `pr/61-live` removes Edge with no replacement (base `.browserstack.yml` had chrome/safari/firefox/edge; head has chrome/playwright-webkit/playwright-firefox + 3 real mobile devices), AND `.docs/architecture.md` at live head still states the desktop matrix includes Edge, AND this PR edited that architecture.md line without correcting the content.
**Attack it:** is `playwright-webkit`/`playwright-firefox` a rename of the same coverage? Can Playwright even drive Edge on BrowserStack (check whether an `msedge` channel option exists in this setup)? If Edge is technically unsupported for Playwright runs, the finding changes from "coverage silently dropped" to "coverage was never achievable this way" — determine which.

**C19.** At `pr/61-live`, `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s relevance check sets `relevant=true` unless an `e2e-scope.json` artifact exists AND its `.e2e` field is `"false"` — i.e. it FAILS OPEN onto a paid BrowserStack run when the artifact is missing/unreadable. And `qa.yml` uploads that artifact with `retention-days: 1`, so a Deploy Preview re-run >24h later fails open.
Verify both, at live head (the newer commit touched this file — check whether the fail-open was changed).

**C20 — verify a claim made from CI logs.** A prior reviewer claimed that under `browserstack-node-sdk`, the SDK cross-multiplies Playwright projects by configured platforms, so the MOBILE spec executed on `OSX Sonoma` and `Windows 11`, and `--grep @SFCC-751` matching 12 local tests produced 60 BrowserStack instances. Evidence cited: run `32805482849`, job `97674692941`.
**Verify independently** via `gh api` / `gh run view --log` for that run. Does the log actually show that? If you cannot retrieve the log, say so — do NOT accept the claim on the prior reviewer's word.

**C21.** `browserstack-node-sdk` appears in NEITHER `package.json` nor `package-lock.json` at `pr/61-live`, yet is invoked via bare `npx` in the workflows — so the `npm ci --ignore-scripts` hardening added in the newest commit is followed by an unpinned registry download-and-execute in the same job with secrets in scope. Verify each part; state search scope inline.

**C22.** `BasePage.js` at `pr/61-live` replaced an accessible-name selector (`getByRole('button', {name: /decline tracking/i})` at base) with a CSS class selector (`.chakra-modal__body button:visible`) and takes `.first()`, assuming decline precedes accept in DOM order — so if that order ever flips, the suite silently ACCEPTS tracking.
**Attack it:** is there any guard that verifies the button's identity (text/aria) rather than just counting? Is the base version really what I claim? Does anything downstream assert consent state?

**C23.** Seven E2E secrets referenced in CI do not exist: `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`. Verify via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/actions/secrets` and the relevant environment secrets endpoints. Note secret VALUES are not readable but NAMES are. Also determine whether this is pre-existing (check base) or introduced by this PR.

=== OUTPUT ===
Per claim: verdict, exact evidence, "what would falsify this", whether attempted, corrected wording if PARTIALLY PROVEN. End with a list of any claim that is technically true but where the CONSEQUENCE I stated does not follow — those are the most dangerous to post.

# ── Environment switching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This file is the documented template for every variable the project uses. Each
# active line below is preceded by its own `# scope:shared`, `# scope:tier`,
# `# scope:personal`, or `# scope:auto` comment line (parsed by
# scripts/switchEnv.mjs, ignored by everything else — kept on its own line,
# not trailing on the KEY=value line, so a blank placeholder here still reads
# as genuinely empty to the pre-commit secret guard):
#   scope:shared   — same value across all 6 tiers (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod)
#                    AND same for the whole team. Lives in .env.shared; included
#                    in `push`/`init`'s pull to/from GitHub Environments.
#   scope:tier     — differs per tier. Lives in the gitignored .env.<tier> for
#                    whichever tier you're pointing local dev at; also
#                    included in `push`/pull.
#   scope:personal — tier-independent like shared, but a PERSONAL credential
#                    (your own Atlassian token, your own Contentful CMA token)
#                    that must never be centralized — still lives in
#                    .env.shared, but `push`/`init`'s pull skip it entirely.
#                    Each developer fills this in themselves.
#   scope:auto     — never hand-set; scripts/switchEnv.mjs injects this itself.
#
# A second optional tag `# mrt:true` marks variables that belong in the MRT
# Managed Runtime environment (storefront runtime config). Only keys tagged
# `mrt:true` are synced by the "Sync Env Vars to MRT" GitHub Actions workflow.
# CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
# are NOT tagged — they are never synced to MRT.
#
# Commands (see scripts/switchEnv.mjs for details):
#   npm run env -- init       — scaffold .env.shared + every .env.<tier> at once,
#                                so you can fill in all tokens in one pass instead
#                                of tier by tier
#   npm run env -- validate   — check all existing env files: unknown/misplaced
#                                keys, blanks, and cross-checks (e.g. a tier's

#                                tier's config/<tier>.js proxy host)
#   npm run env -- validate --live — also makes a real read-only Contentful
#                                Delivery API call AND a real SLAS guest
#                                (client_credentials) token request per tier —
#                                confirms credentials actually work, not just
#                                that they're set. The SLAS check is the same
#                                request every anonymous shopper visit already
#                                triggers — no customer/commerce data touched.
#   npm run env -- push <shared|dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod> — tier-1-approvers

# plaintext and readable by any repo collaborator (no per-key ACL like
# CODEOWNERS gives files) — they do not meet the bar AGENTS.md's "secrets only
# in .env / Managed Runtime" rule sets. Using them here anyway was a conscious,
# confirmed tradeoff for centralization; write access is restricted to repo
# Admin (= tier-1-approvers), read access is repo-collaborator-wide by design.
#

# never auto-fetched from SFCC itself — there's no discovery API, and SLAS
# client secrets can't be read back after creation. Those still need a human to
# enter them once (into .env.<tier> or via `push`), but from then on they're
# centrally available via GitHub Environments like everything else here.

# mrt:true
COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU

# browserstack.yml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
# NOTE: named without a leading dot deliberately — browserstack-node-sdk
# searches upward from cwd for exactly `browserstack.yml`; a `.browserstack.yml`
# (this file's name until 2026-08-25) is never found, so every SDK-driven run
# fails at config resolution before any test executes. Confirmed via
# BrowserStack's own docs, and via a real CI failure on PR #61.
# BrowserStack Playwright SDK configuration for cross-browser regression
# Docs: https://www.browserstack.com/docs/automate/playwright/sdk-node

userName: ${BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}
accessKey: ${BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}

# Top-level buildName/projectName govern the classic Automate dashboard's
# build grouping — a different product from Test Observability below, which
# has its own separate projectName/buildName under testObservabilityOptions.
# Without this, Automate showed every run as "Untitled Build Run #N" even
# though testObservabilityOptions.buildName was set correctly (confirmed
# 2026-08-25). Keep both blocks' values in sync.
buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"
projectName: "Zim Project"

framework: playwright

# Zimmermann tests only
testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm

# `platforms:` (with browserName/browserVersion/os/osVersion), not the
# classic Automate/Selenium `browsers:` key (browser/browser_version/
# os/os_version) — the Playwright Node SDK only recognises the former.
# `browsers:` is silently ignored: the SDK finds zero configured
# platforms and every test falls through to a genuine local Playwright
# launch instead of one on BrowserStack's cloud, which fails outright
# in CI since no local browser binaries are installed there (that's
# the SDK's job, remotely) — confirmed against the SDK's own installed
# source (modifyPlaywrightConf.js only ever reads a `platforms` key)
# and BrowserStack's current docs, after every desktop/mobile spec
# failed this exact way on PR #61, 2026-08-25. Safari has no Playwright
# driver of its own — `playwright-webkit` is BrowserStack's mapping for
# testing WebKit-engine (Safari-equivalent) behaviour, same reasoning
# for `playwright-firefox`. `chrome`/`edge` run for real since Playwright
# drives them directly via CDP.
#
# This account's plan allows exactly ONE concurrent BrowserStack session
# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26 — not the account's queue
# ceiling this time, its actual `team_parallel_sessions_max_allowed`).
# Every platform below therefore runs strictly sequentially — platform
# count is a direct multiplier on wall-clock time and cost, with zero
# parallelism benefit from adding more. That ruled out a broad "current
# device − 2 generations" matrix across iPhone/Samsung/Pixel (would have
# been 9 real-mobile platforms alone): on a 1-session plan, what a real
# device buys you is OS/engine-version coverage, not device-generation
# depth — an iPhone 15 and an iPhone 17 on the same iOS build render
# near-identically, so one current device per platform we can't get any
# other way beats three generations of one we can. Six platforms total:
# three real devices (the coverage nothing else in this pipeline can
# provide) plus the three desktop engines already established. Edge and
# a second desktop Chrome OS were cut entirely — same Chromium engine as
# the real Android devices below, lowest marginal value under a strict
# 1-session budget.

  - os: OS X
    osVersion: Sonoma
    browserName: chrome
    browserVersion: latest

  # AU / US / HK significant Safari share (Apple-heavy luxury market) —
  # desktop WebKit signal, distinct from the real iOS Safari device below
  # (different rendering path: desktop vs. mobile Safari).
  - os: OS X
    osVersion: Sonoma
    browserName: playwright-webkit
    browserVersion: latest

  # UK / EU / ME — the other non-Chromium desktop engine.
  - os: Windows
    osVersion: 11
    browserName: playwright-firefox
    browserVersion: latest

  # Real iOS device, real Safari — not Playwright's desktop WebKit build
  # (the entry above), which is a genuine engine but not the same
  # rendering path as Mobile Safari (different scrolling, fixed-position,
  # and viewport behaviour). BrowserStack added real-device Playwright
  # Safari support industry-first, June 2025 — confirmed current via
  # browserstack.com/guide/playwright-ios-automation and BrowserStack's
  # own docs (2026-08-26). Current model, iPhone 17, on its ship OS,
  # iOS 26 (confirmed live via web search, not training data — iPhone 17
  # launched Sept 2025 with iOS 26 pre-installed). deviceName + osVersion
  # + browserName: safari + realMobile: true is BrowserStack's documented
  # real-device shape (no `os:` field, matching the Android entries'
  # shape below) — not yet live-verified against this account's actual
  # device catalogue (local `.env` BrowserStack creds are blank, so this
  # couldn't be checked from here); confirm on the next real CI run.
  - deviceName: iPhone 17
    osVersion: '26'
    browserName: safari
    realMobile: true

  # Real Android device, Samsung — Samsung's One UI skin/GPU stack is a
  # meaningfully different rendering environment from stock Android.
  # Current model, Galaxy S26, on its ship OS: Android 16 / One UI 8.5
  # (confirmed live via web search, 2026-08-26). Not yet live-verified
  # against the device catalogue, same caveat as above.
  - deviceName: Samsung Galaxy S26
    osVersion: '16.0'
    browserName: chrome
    realMobile: true

  # Real Android device, Pixel — stock Android reference device, the
  # other real-world Android profile Zimmermann's Android traffic splits
  # across alongside Samsung. Current model, Pixel 11, on its ship OS:
  # Android 17 (confirmed live via web search, 2026-08-26) — launched
  # 2026-08-20, six days before this config was written, so there's a
  # real chance BrowserStack hasn't onboarded physical units yet; if the
  # next CI run can't find this device, fall back to Pixel 10 (Android 16)
  # until BrowserStack's catalogue catches up.

    osVersion: '17.0'
    browserName: chrome
    realMobile: true

# .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml (SFCC-751) to sync Zephyr Scale
# execution records. Not BrowserStack's native Zephyr link — that only
# supports US/EU API regions and this org's Zephyr instance is DE-hosted, so
# results are synced via our own workflow instead. projectName matches the
# real BrowserStack project ("Zim Project", id 2664550) — confirmed via a
# live GET /ext/v1/projects call on 2026-08-25 that no "Zimmermann-PWA"
# project exists in this account.

testObservabilityOptions:
  projectName: "Zim Project"
  buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"

# This account's plan allows exactly 1 concurrent BrowserStack session
# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26) — parallelsPerPlatform can
# only ever be 1 here; anything higher requests more concurrent sessions
# than the plan allows and risks [BROWSERSTACK_QUEUE_SIZE_EXCEEDED] again
# (first hit at 10 concurrent, 2026-08-25, when this was 5 platforms x 2).

  buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"

     1	name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
     2	
     3	# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
     4	# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
     5	# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
     6	# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
     7	# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
     8	# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
     9	# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
    10	# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
    11	# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
    12	# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
    13	#
    14	# release/** PRs are unaffected — deploy-preview.yml never runs for
    15	# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
    16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
    17	#
    18	# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
    19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
    20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
    21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
    22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.
    23	on:
    24	  workflow_run:
    25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
    26	    types: [completed]
    27	
    28	permissions:
    29	  contents: read
    30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
    31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch
    32	
    33	jobs:
    34	  e2e-browserstack:
    35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    37	    # A cancelled Deploy Preview run skips this job entirely (there's
    38	    # nothing to test and no hostname artifact could exist). Any other
    39	    # conclusion still runs -- if Deploy Preview failed rather than
    40	    # succeeded, "Resolve BrowserStack test target" below fails the job
    41	    # loudly instead of silently testing an unrelated environment (see
    42	    # that step's own comment for why the old test-tier fallback was
    43	    # removed, CodeRabbit, 2026-08-26).
    44	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    45	    timeout-minutes: 25
    46	    environment: test # for the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
    47	    steps:
    48	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
    49	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
    50	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
    51	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
    52	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
    53	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
    54	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
    55	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
    56	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
    57	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
    58	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
    59	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    60	        with:
    61	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
    62	
    63	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    64	        with:
    65	          node-version: '24'
    66	          cache: 'npm'
    67	
    68	      # --ignore-scripts, not --include=dev with lifecycle scripts enabled:
    69	      # this job checks out and executes a PR branch's own code with real
    70	      # BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_*/E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets in scope, and
    71	      # workflow_run grants those secrets unconditionally -- unlike
    72	      # pull_request, there is no pending-approval gate here even for a
    73	      # same-repo branch. Without --ignore-scripts, anyone with push access

    76	      # in between (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26). Skipping

    78	      # app locally (it only drives Playwright against an already-deployed
    79	      # preview), so it doesn't need postinstall's translation-compilation
    80	      # or registry-generation side effects.

    82	        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
    83

    85	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
    86	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.

    90	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    91	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}

   182	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

content.content:
=== testing.md 'Access-gated preview URLs' section @ live ===
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
